explain.say: Imagine juggling ten balls at once: homework, a test, a fight with a friend and chores. They all start falling! That "it is all too much" feeling is called being overwhelmed. Look at the plan. Step one: stop and breathe.

faq.a: Being overwhelmed means feeling there is too much to handle at once, so you do not know where to start. You might feel frozen, teary, cross or want to hide.

faq.q: Why does writing a list help when I feel overwhelmed?
faq.a: Your brain can only hold a few things at once. Writing everything down frees up space, and you can see the tasks clearly instead of feeling them as one huge pile.

faq.q: How do I decide what to do first?
faq.a: Pick the thing that is due soonest or matters most. If you are stuck, ask a teacher or parent to help you choose.
asks: Where do I start when I have too much homework?

faq.q: Who can help when I have too much to do?
faq.a: A parent or carer, a teacher, an older sibling or a friend. Teachers can sometimes give extra time or help you plan if you tell them early.
asks: Can my teacher help if I am overwhelmed?

faq.q: What if I feel overwhelmed all the time?
faq.a: If you feel this way most days, talk to a trusted grown-up, a school counsellor or a doctor. You may have too much on, and they can help you make changes.
asks: I always feel like everything is too much

facts: Psychologist Nelson Cowan found that working memory can hold only about four chunks of information at once.
In a 2018 study at Baylor University, people who wrote a to-do list for five minutes before bed fell asleep faster than those who wrote about tasks they had finished.

quiz.why: A tiny first step is easy to begin, and progress builds from there.
